scope: Algebra-only audit of the stated positive-parameter matrix assumptions. No new matrix benchmark, PDE/GPU candidate or performance measurement.

checks.reason: If M and K are symmetric positive semidefinite and a_ref M + h_ref K is positive definite for positive reference coefficients, their nullspaces have trivial intersection. Every positive a_j M + h_j K is therefore positive definite.

H whitening followed by orthogonal diagonalization of the whitened M gives P^T H P=I and theta_i=a_ref lambda_i in [0,1]. The complementary h_ref K diagonal is 1-theta_i, so the phase diagonal formula is exact.
After factoring a_j/a_ref, each diagonal entry is theta_i + (r_j/eta)(1-theta_i). Its ratio of largest to smallest is at most max(1,r_j/eta)/min(1,r_j/eta)=max(r_j/eta,eta/r_j).

The worst bound equals max(r_max/eta,eta/r_min). The two terms have fixed product r_max/r_min, so their maximum is at least its square root, with equality exactly at eta=sqrt(r_min*r_max) (also when the endpoints coincide).

This minimizes the stated worst-case bound, not necessarily the actual condition number for a particular spectrum. Common reference scaling cancels from the condition bound. It does not force every d_ji near one, control the original coordinates, fix cross-mode noncommutativity, establish time-integration stability or establish runtime savings.

publication_note: The earlier matrix and timing evidence remains unchanged; report this only as a mathematical correction and anchor-selection bound.
